headline: The lab's label machinery is sound. Next-open entry, NaN handling, segment and suspension guards, ISIN identity, corporate-action adjustment and all point-in-time features passed independent checks (360/360 feature recomputations matched, including rows with later splits). The walk-forward harness catches leaks: shuffled labels give cross-sectional AUC 0.500, and one day of look-ahead gives 0.63-0.65. One high-severity leak: sectors.parquet is a 2026 snapshot, and sec_rel_mom20 carries it into the models. "Has a sector" names earn +56 bps per 10-day trade (t=5.6) in every year 2021-25 and only +12 bps in 2026. Sorting on sec_rel_mom20 is the #1 and #2 best of 106 single-feature strategies on 2023-25, with either sign, and both fail in 2026. Three medium issues: ETFs are 3.5% of elig_base; portfolio_sim overstates Sharpe 12-24% and understates maxDD 2.6-3.3pp; duplicate exchange corporate-action records double-apply 7 splits and 30 dividends. Bias budget at h=10: +27 bps phantom close-entry edge; 45% of split windows flip sign on raw prices; monthly P(up) ranges 21-69% (corr 0.66 with market); 1.35M rows carry only ~1,000 independent observations. Luck band: random 20 picks every 5 days at 50 bps made 1.7% ± 3.2% CAGR in 2023-25 against Nifty 500's 15.5%, because costs take about 12.6%/yr. A model with zero selection skill reaches 4.9%, so candidates must beat the persistent-tilt p95 of 8.4% CAGR. The leak-free reference absolute label clears dev (15.5% CAGR) but fails the 2026 holdout (-6.9% vs random -6.5%).

ENTITY BRIDGING passes. 264 pure renames: adjusted move on the switch day has median 1.15% and max 11.7%, none above 20%. 341 ISIN-change bridges: 323 coincide with an applied split or bonus (median |adj move| 3.6% vs raw 77.5%). 22 bridges show an adjusted move above 20%: 15 are missing corporate-action records (SHRIRAMFIN 2025-01-10, 360ONE, WEL, SBGLP, MOTISONS, DAVANGERE, NAVKARURB, DOLPHIN, AGIIL, 6 ETFs), 4 are double-applied factors (HAL, LIKHITHA, RPPL, AJMERA), and 3 are genuine +20% upper-circuit days after a split. The 19 defective ones are all label-blocked. The 7 'symbol reuse' cases (BURNPUR, EASTSILK, KAUSHALYA, MBECL, SHEKHAWATI, SUMEETINDS, VERTOZ) are all the same issuer relisting with a new ISIN after a consolidation or long gap. They are correctly not merged, but no cross-company symbol reuse exists in the data, so that guard is untested. 427 entities end early, so the universe is not survivorship-filtered.

CORPORATE ACTIONS pass, with defects. Of 20 sampled splits/bonuses, raw moves of -26% to -90% become adjusted moves of -5% to +11% (one exception, HAL +97%, from double application). Across 571 split/bonus rows: median |raw move| 66.8%, median |adj move| 4.3% (normal day 1.3%), and 20 of the 45 cases above 15% are exactly +20% upper-circuit closes (genuine). Dividends: 8,717 applied, median yield 0.54%, p99 9.9%, median 0.67% per entity-year. The adjusted series is close to total return while Nifty 500 is a price index. Rights: 162 applied (median factor 0.93), 15 blocked. The 459 label_block rows come from residual jumps above 35% (323), exchange block keywords such as 67 demergers (86), prev-close gaps (27) and other causes (23). Only 81 adjusted moves above 25% remain unblocked, mostly listings, relistings and BE series; they touch only 26 valid h=10 windows (0.002%).

POINT-IN-TIME passes. I checked 12 features (mom_20, mom_60, dist_sma50, vol_20, rsi_14, volz_20, deliv_z20, hi52_dist, beta_60, atr_pct, max_ret_20, gap_open) on 30 rows, 15 of them with a split later in the segment. Each was recomputed from data truncated at t and re-adjusted with only the corporate-action factors known at t: 360/360 match. Max relative difference is 6e-8, or 6e-5 for volz_20 because of log1p. Back-adjustment does not leak because all features are scale-invariant ratios. Index/panel alignment is perfect: 1,434 = 1,434 sessions, and the median stock return correlates 0.886 with the index at lag 0 vs 0.06/0.005 at lag ±1. elig_next uses look-ahead but only excludes 41 rows (0.003%) outside the last date.

HIGH-SEVERITY LEAK in the sector map. sectors.parquet holds today's (2026) Nifty Total Market constituents, 748 entities. Sector-known vs NA, 10-day forward return, date-demeaned: +38.7, +53.2, +76.4, +68.2 and +72.9 bps in 2021-2025, falling to +9.2 bps in 2026. Pooled it is +56 bps per trade, t=5.6 on non-overlapping dates, and it holds within every liquidity tercile. Ranking on sec_rel_mom20, which is NaN for 43% of rows, is the #1 and #2 of 106 single-feature strategies on 2023-25 with either sign (Sharpe 1.04 and 0.69) and fails in 2026 (-0.07 and 0.14). In the walk-forward model, dropping sec_rel_mom20 reduces the cross-sectional AUC edge by 16-34% in every year. It also cuts the share of picks with a 2026 sector from 82.5% to 68%; the universe share is 56.7%. D_setups' 'sector leader' setup and B_relative's sector-relative label with market-excess fallback for NA names inherit this leak.

CANARIES. Label: 1{open[t+1]->close[t+10] > 50bps}, walk_forward with date_step=2. 'XS-AUC' below is the mean per-date (cross-sectional) AUC. Shuffling the label within each date gives XS-AUC 0.499/0.499/0.500/0.501 for 2023/24/25/26, but pooled AUC 0.521/0.545/0.488/0.544. The real model's pooled AUC is 0.523/0.568/0.494/0.549, so pooled AUC on absolute labels is almost entirely market timing; teams must report cross-sectional AUC or IC. A forward-return-plus-noise feature gives XS-AUC 0.77-0.80 (t 39-49) and 8,368% CAGR. A single day of look-ahead (day-1 intraday return) gives XS-AUC 0.63-0.65 (t 16-24), Sharpe 10.8 and 543% CAGR. The harness detects leakage at every strength tested.

BIAS BUDGET, h=10 and h=20 on elig_base. Close vs next-open entry: +27.3 bps phantom edge per trade at both horizons (2021: 42, 2025: 17); 4.0% of labels flip at h=10 and 2.9% at h=20. Unadjusted prices: 4.2% of h10 windows contain a corporate action and 0.20% a split; 44.5% of split windows flip sign; mean raw return in split windows is -62.8% vs +0.25% adjusted; split windows are 20% (h10) and 40% (h20) of the raw bottom-1% tail; dividend windows differ by +87 bps. NaN->0: excluding the data tail, 0.085% of rows at h10 (0.17% at h20) are undefined, but their forced-exit outcome averages -15.8%. Ticker-keyed vs entity-keyed: 780 windows fragmented at renames, 10,149 eligible rows lost to the seasoning reset, 0 cross-company splices. Threshold 0 vs 50 bps: 6.6% of 'up' labels lose money after cost; flat share is 6.6% at ±50 bps and 10.4% at ±80 bps. Survivorship: survivors-only inflates the 2021-23 mean 10-day return by only +1.3 bps, because non-survivors are 1.6% of eligible rows.

REGIME AND EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE. Absolute label h10 (>50bps): monthly P(up) mean 45.5%, sd 13.1%, range 20.8%-69.0%, corr 0.66 with the Nifty monthly return. By regime it is 48-50% in bear and 43-44% in bull. By year: 46.0/43.6/51.1/44.5/42.1/42.7% (2021-26). The market-excess label has monthly sd 6.4% and corr 0.08. Overlap: label lag-1 autocorrelation is 0.70 (h10) and 0.79 (h20), giving design effects of 7.05 and 14.6. Within-date ICC is 0.18, so the cross-sectional design effect is about 188. N_eff by label: absolute ~1,021 (h10) and 491 (h20); market-excess 3,722 and 1,895; cross-sectional top-30% rank ~183k (an upper bound). Use date-clustered or non-overlapping inference.

LUCK BAND. Setup: h=10, top-20, step 5, 20 seeds, 2023-01-01..2025-12-31. iid random at 50 bps: CAGR 1.66% ± 3.21% (p5 -4.3%, p95 5.5%), Sharpe 0.18 ± 0.22 (p95 0.44), maxDD -29%. At 80 bps: -5.6% ± 3.0%. 2026 holdout: -6.5% ± 5.9% at 50 bps and -13.1% at 80 bps. Nifty 500: 15.5% over 2023-25 and -5.7% in 2026. Costs dominate: about 25 round trips per year x 50 bps is roughly 12.6%/yr of drag. A persistent random tilt (fixed random score per entity) is the right null for sticky model picks: CAGR 0.7% ± 5.85% (p95 8.4%), Sharpe sd 0.39 (p95 0.64). The shuffled zero-skill model's 4.9% CAGR and 0.37 Sharpe sit inside that band. Random by year: 2023 +27.9%, 2024 -1.7%, 2025 -16.2%. Six 3-seed averages range from -0.5% to +4.3%.

SELECTION SHRINKAGE (factor zoo). 106 strategies: each of the 53 lab features with both signs, 50 bps. Dev Sharpe p95 0.48, max 1.04, and the max is the sec_rel_mom20 leak. The top-5 on dev have mean Sharpe 0.68 in dev and 0.02 in 2026. Spearman correlation between dev and 2026 Sharpe is 0.11 (p=0.26), so dev rankings barely persist out of sample.

PORTFOLIO_SIM STATISTICS ARE OPTIMISTIC. It books each cohort's full h-day return on the signal date, and its two overlapping sleeves make step returns autocorrelated (lag-1 0.31). Against a daily mark-to-market rebuild with identical picks and identical final equity: random baselines show sim Sharpe 0.306 vs MTM 0.278 and maxDD -28.6% vs -31.2%; the walk-forward model in 2023-25 shows Sharpe 1.03 vs 0.83 and maxDD -30.7% vs -34.0%. The Nifty benchmark Sharpe uses daily returns, so it is not comparable with sim Sharpe.

MULTIPLE-TESTING PROTOCOL. (1) Open the 2026 holdout once, for at most 3 pre-registered finalists. (2) End dev signals at the last date with t+h <= 2025-12-31. (3) Count N team-wide and report it. (4) Use cross-sectional AUC/IC with non-overlapping t-stats, plus excess CAGR and MTM Sharpe over a random baseline of at least 10 seeds from the same mask; never use pooled AUC. (5) Minimum effect: XS-AUC >= 0.52 (IC >= 0.03), t >= 3, above 0.5 in each dev year, and positive excess at 80 bps and in at least 2 of 3 years. (6) Luck hurdle from the persistent-tilt null: dev CAGR above 8.4%, and sim-Sharpe above mu + sigma x Phi^-1(0.95^(1/N)), which is 1.01/1.10/1.19/1.30/1.38 for N=5/10/20/50/100 (iid null: 0.69/0.74/0.79/0.85/0.90; MTM hurdles roughly 0.85-0.9x). (7) Plan for at least a 50% haircut on dev excess. (8) Leak tripwires: XS-AUC above 0.58, top-decile 10-day excess above 300 bps, or Sharpe above 3.

REFERENCE ABSOLUTE LABEL (leak-free features). Dev 2023-25: CAGR 15.5%, sim Sharpe 0.95, maxDD -28.5%, 7.2% at 80 bps; by year +36.1%, +24.6%, -9.0%. It clears the persistent band but only marginally clears the deflated-Sharpe hurdle for N=1. 2026: -6.9% vs random -6.5%, so it fails the holdout. Top-decile 10-day return in 2026 is 30 bps vs the universe's 33 bps. F&O shorts beat random shorts (dev -21.0% vs -27.1%; 2026 +1.6% vs -18.2%) but still lose money in dev. The binding constraints for the team are regime dependence, effective sample size and transaction costs, not data leakage.
lab_issues_found: HIGH: sectors.parquet is a 2026 snapshot of Nifty Total Market constituents (748 entities), creating look-ahead and survivorship bias through the feature sec_rel_mom20 (its NaN-ness), F.sector, sector-relative labels and sector-gated setups. Evidence: +56 bps per 10-day trade for sector-known names (t=5.6) in every year 2021-25, +12 bps in 2026; ±sec_rel_mom20 are the top-2 of 106 dev strategies and fail in 2026; model picks are 82.5% sector-known vs 68% without the feature. FIX: remove sec_rel_mom20 from L.FEATURES; never use sector or its NaN-ness as a feature, filter, setup or label split; treat NA as one capped bucket in max_per_sector; rebuild a point-in-time sector map if sectors are needed.

MEDIUM: ETFs and mutual-fund units (ISIN INF..., e.g. GOLDBEES, SILVERBEES, NIFTYBEES, MON100) are inside elig_base: 48,406 rows (3.5%), 130 instruments, rising to about 5% in 2025-26. They also appear in 2,504 fno_proxy rows and feed the xr_*, breadth and dispersion features. The shuffled model put 10% of its 2026 picks into ETFs. FIX: require ISIN prefix 'INE' and recompute cross-sectional features on equities only.

MEDIUM: portfolio_sim books cohort P&L at the signal date, and its overlapping sleeves autocorrelate step returns (lag-1 0.31). Result: Sharpe overstated by about 1.12x (random) and 1.24x (model); maxDD too shallow by 2.6-3.3pp; by_year shifted by h days. The Nifty benchmark Sharpe is daily, so the two are not comparable. FIX: build a daily mark-to-market equity curve (s6_sim_audit.py::mtm) and book P&L at exit.

MEDIUM: duplicate exchange book-closure records whose ex-dates differ by 1-7 days are applied twice. 7 splits/bonuses are double-applied: HAL 2023-09-28 gets factor 0.25 instead of 0.5 (+97% fake jump, label-blocked), AJMERA 0.04 instead of 0.2, and AKSHAR's 1:5 bonus produces a +17% fake jump that is NOT blocked. 30 dividends are applied twice (median extra 0.53%). FIX: de-duplicate events per (entity, kind, desc) within ±7 days before locating them.

MEDIUM-LOW: the corporate-action archive is missing some splits and demergers (SHRIRAMFIN 5:1 Jan-2025, 360ONE, SIEMENS demerger Apr-2025, WEL, SBGLP, MOTISONS, DAVANGERE, NAVKARURB, DOLPHIN, AGIIL, ETF splits). There are 76 unadjusted split-like jumps; all are label-blocked, so labels are safe. Features are not: 1.1% of eligible rows (1.9% of fno_proxy rows) have long-lookback features (mom_60/120, mom_12_1, hi52/lo52_dist, dist_sma200, vol_60, beta_60) whose window spans a block. FIX: infer the factor when a residual jump coincides with an ISIN change, or set those features to NaN when their window spans a label_block row.

LOW: walk_forward scores only rows with a defined label, so model picks can never land on future-suspended, delisted or demerger windows, while random picks can (0.082% of picks, mean -5.9%). This gives any model strategy about +0.15pp/yr of free CAGR. Those undefined windows have a mean forced-exit outcome of -15.8%. FIX: predict on all mask rows and compute metrics only on labeled rows.

LOW: elig_next uses look-ahead (it checks that t+1 trades). Apart from the last panel date it excludes only 41 rows (0.003%), whose next-bar mean is -8.9%. FIX: drop it, since labels are already NaN when t+1 is missing.

LOW: dividend and rights parser gaps. 540 of 9,511 dividend-like records are unparsed ('INTERIM DIVIDEND' or 'DIVIDEND' with no amount; 'AGM/DIV-20 SPLDIV-15' with no 'RS'). 'RIGHTS 1:10 PRM RS 194/-' without '@' is blocked. The rights-adjusted price uses today's face value, which is stale for 16 rights events that had a later split. FIX: parse bare amounts, accept PRM without '@', and use the face value as of the event date.

LOW: three hygiene items. The dev window end='2025-12-31' lets trades exit in Jan-2026; end dev signals where t+h <= 2025-12-31. A within-date shuffled label reproduces the pooled AUC (0.521/0.545/0.488/0.544 vs the real 0.523/0.568/0.494/0.549). headline: Correctly built triple-barrier labels are bias-free and their classes match realized P&L, but they mostly track the market: on a given day the share of +1 labels runs from 17% to 82%, with 0.72 correlation to the Nifty 500 return over the same window. Cross-sectionally they are only weakly learnable (xs-AUC 0.53 in 2023-25) and no more learnable than a path-blind 20-day label built the same way. Executing the barrier, specifically the stop, destroys value. Recommended spec within this family, selected on 2023-25 only: A1 = h=20, target and stop each 2.0 x ATR14%, entry at next open, +/-50 bp dead zone at the time barrier. Event rates: +1 48.9% / -1 49.6% / 0 1.6%. Use it only as a ranking target with a 20-day time exit: 2023-25 CAGR 26.1% vs 11.1% for random picks and 15.5% for Nifty 500. In the 2026 holdout it made +3.9% vs +2.9% random, and the per-trade edge was about 0 (t 0.06). Verdict: weak.

candidates.family: triple barrier, fixed daily-ATR multiples (absolute, path-dependent)
candidates.definition: Signal at close[t], entry open[t+1]. Target = entry*(1+2.0*atr_pct[t]) (median +7.3%), stop = entry*(1-2.0*atr_pct[t]). Scans bars t+1..t+20. Stop is checked before target on the same bar; a gap through a barrier fills at that bar's open. Time exit at close[t+20]. +1 = target first, or time-exit return > +50 bp. -1 = stop first, or time-exit return < -50 bp. 0 = time exit within +/-50 bp. NaN where fw.ok(20) is false. Model: LightGBM binary (+1 vs rest), L.walk_forward with date_step=2. Portfolio numbers below use the recommended 20-day time exit; barrier-exit numbers are in cons.
candidates.horizon: 20 trading days max (mean 9.7 bars held; median 7 bars to target or stop)
candidates.sides: long (short mirror measured: unconditional net expectancy negative, all F&O short books lost money)
candidates.holdout_2026_note: Jan to 10 Sep 2026 (Nifty -4.0%): time-exit book +3.9% vs random +2.9%. Barrier-exit book -0.4% vs random -1.2%. Top-20 excess per 20-day trade +0.07% (t 0.06), down from +1.16% (t 2.57) in 2023-25. The bottom decile still lagged the universe by -0.74%. The holdout does not confirm the edge, and with ~8 months it has low power.
pros: Every class maps to a realized P&L sign (100% coherence at tau=50; 99% of +1 labels still profitable at 80 bp)
85% of labels are decided by a barrier, so the label really is path-aware. Natural holds fall in the 5-20 day window.
Exactly matches lablib.barrier_labels (0 mismatches). Same-bar ambiguity is only 0.07%; gap-through stop 3.3%.
Event rate is flat across liquidity terciles (48.1/48.7/49.8%) and ATR terciles (48.3/49.2/49.0%)
Best of the three geometries on the role's barrier-exit test (2023-25 Sharpe 0.95 vs 0.48 for A2 and 0.01 for A3)
cons: Mostly market direction: daily corr with the same-window Nifty return is 0.72; the daily +1 share runs 17-82% (5th-95th pct); monthly corr 0.65
Executing the barrier itself loses: 2023-25 CAGR 6.0% (Sharpe 0.95) vs Nifty 15.5%; 2.0% at 80 bp. Random barrier book -5.5%. Gross return per day held is 1.0 bp vs 6.6 bp for a 20-day hold.
The stop is what hurts. Target-only exit: Sharpe 2.25 with maxDD -15.8%. Stop-only: Sharpe 1.24.
No more learnable than the path-blind 20d control label (control xs-AUC 0.532/0.552/0.548)
Pooled AUC falls below 0.5 in 2023 and 2025 because the model's implicit market call was wrong
Overlap is heavy: lag-1 ACF 0.73, variance inflation about 11
The 2026 holdout edge is about 0

key_findings: REPORT.md was NOT written. The harness rejected the subagent's Write of a .md report file ('Subagents should return findings as text'), and I did not work around it. The full findings are in this structured output. All tables and numbers are on disk in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-SuryaDhana-AI/09834923-517b-5951-ac02-867e5810ca36/scratchpad/lab/results/A_barrier/: results.json (every number plus a summary block), curated_tables.json (ready-made markdown tables keyed by section: geom_long_h5/10/15/20, geom_short_*, tau_long, shortlist_events, shortlist_regime, exit_econ, time_exit_uncond, invest_summary, gate_short, significance, nifty), tables_autogen.md (machine-generated tables for all 144 configs and per-model investability), grid.csv, events_shortlist.json, invest_*.json, variants_*.json, significance.json, compare_learnability.json. The lead can assemble REPORT.md from curated_tables.json.

Validation: the vectorized barrier engine (abar.py) reproduces L.barrier_labels exactly on two configurations: h10 long fixed 2/1.5 (1,351,823 rows) and h20 short sqrt 1/0.75 (1,337,462 rows). Both had 0 label mismatches, 0 NaN-pattern mismatches and max |return diff| = 0. All portfolio sims call unmodified lablib.portfolio_sim.

Geometry: ATR14% (median 3.7%) is about 1.3-1.5x the daily close-to-close sigma. As a result, every sqrt(h)-scaled geometry with a,b >= 0.75 ends at the time barrier 52-91% of the time, at every h. They are path-blind sign labels in disguise. The D_setups common label (h10, 1.5/1.0 x ATR x sqrt10) resolves 6.4% target / 11.3% stop / 82.3% time. Fixed daily-ATR multiples at h >= 15 are genuinely path-dependent: 72-95% resolved by a touch, median 5-9 bars to touch, mean hold 6.7-14.4 bars. At h=5 every geometry is >= 54% time exits.

Event rates: with tau=50 every long geometry at h >= 10 gives P(+1) of 37-61%. Touch-only (+1 = target hit) gives 6-58%, and sqrt a=1.5 is too rare at 6-7%. Moving tau 0 -> 100 bp lowers P(+1) by only 0.8-1.5 pp for fixed h=20 geometries but by 4-6 pp for sqrt ones. Parameter map at h=20: raising pt 1.5 -> 3 ATR moves P(target) 47.7 -> 26.5% and P(+1) 49.1 -> 36.7%. Raising sl 1.5 -> 3 moves P(+1) 49.1 -> 61.0%. Going h 10 -> 20 (2/2) moves the resolved share 61 -> 85%.

Coherence: at tau=50 every +1 nets positive at 50 bp (net given +1 between +4.0% and +9.7%) and every -1 nets negative. At tau=0, 90-99% of +1 labels are profitable. At 80 bp, 97-99% of +1 labels (h >= 10) remain profitable. Same-bar ambiguity is 0.00-0.10% (immaterial). Gap-through-stop fills affect 1-4% of rows.

Regime dependence (the absolute-label problem): for A1, the daily cross-sectional share of +1 runs from 16.8% to 81.5% (5th-95th pct). It correlates 0.72 with the Nifty 500 return over the same executable window (0.84-0.87 for time-dominated sqrt labels). Monthly P(+1) ranges 25.1% (Jan-2025) to 76.6% (Jul-2022), with std 14.5pp, corr 0.65 with same-month and 0.74 with same+next-month index return. By year: 50.3/47.0/57.8/46.4/45.3/48.1 (2021-26). The PIT regime tag works the other way: P(+1) is 53-54% when Nifty is below its 200-dma vs 47% above, because 2021-26 bear phases were followed by rebounds. Liquidity terciles are nearly flat (48.1/48.7/49.8). F&O proxy 50.4%.

Overlap: lag-1 ACF of the label is 0.67-0.73, lag-5 0.25-0.40, about 0 beyond h. Variance inflation (1 + 2*sum of rho) is about 6 at h=10 and 11 at h=20, so the effective sample is about 1/11 of rows.

Exit economics drive the investability of the whole family. Unconditional gross return per day held in 2023-25 was 1.0 bp for a 2/2 ATR barrier vs 6.6 bp for a 20-day time exit. Unconditional net per trade (50 bp) was -0.40% for the barrier vs +0.82% for the 20d hold. Wider stops monotonically raise expectancy (h20 1.5/1.5 -> 1.5/3.0: -0.50% -> -0.22%). Random-pick books, 2023-25 CAGR: barrier 2/2 -5.5%, stop-only -1.2%, target-only +4.9%, time exit +11.1%. The stop is the value destroyer.

Learnability (6 walk-forward runs: A1 binary, A2 binary, A3 binary, A1 multiclass, A1 without market features, path-blind control). Pooled walk_forward AUC is dominated by the date-level timing component: A1 pooled 0.499/0.564/0.485/0.541 vs date-mean-only 'timing AUC' 0.482/0.555/0.471/0.541. Per-date cross-sectional AUC is positive every year at 0.527/0.544/0.530/0.513. 2023-25 mean xs-AUC: A1 0.534, A2 0.532, A3 0.527, multiclass 0.533 (no gain), no-market 0.533. Top-decile P(+1) lift for A1 is +2.8/+4.3/+3.0 pp. IC vs executable 20d return is 0.05-0.10 (non-overlapping t 2.1-5.9) in 2023-25 and 0.048 (t 1.6) in 2026.

Path dependence adds no learnability. The path-blind control (20d sign, +/-50 bp, next-open entry, NaN-safe) has 2023-25 xs-AUC 0.532/0.552/0.548, IC vs 20d return 0.053/0.099/0.101 and top-decile lift +3.2/+4.9/+5.3 pp, equal to or better than A1 in every selection year. Its 2023-25 time-exit book is the best: 27.6% CAGR, Sharpe 2.46.

Selection (2023-25 only). A1 (h20 2/2) was best on the barrier-exit test the role specifies: Sharpe 0.95 vs A2 0.48 vs A3 0.01. It tied A2 on time exits (2.21 vs 2.18). A3 was clearly worst. So A1 is the recommended spec and A2 the alternative. The 2026 holdout was never used.

Investability, A1 (top-20, step 5). Barrier exit: 2023-25 CAGR 6.0%, Sharpe 0.95 (random -5.5%, Nifty 15.5%/1.20); 2.0% at 80 bp. Time exit: 26.1%, Sharpe 2.21 (random 11.1%/1.09); 21.5% at 80 bp. Full period 2023-01..2026-09: CAGR 21.2%, Sharpe 1.90, maxDD -23.5%. Target-only (no stop): 17.5%, Sharpe 2.25, maxDD -15.8%. Stop-only: 11.9%, Sharpe 1.24. Sector cap 4 makes no difference. top_k 10/20/40 (barrier exit): 6.9/6.0/2.7%. 2025 is the weak year for every long book (A1 time exit +1.2%).

Holdout 2026 (Jan to 10 Sep, Nifty -4.0%): A1 time exit +3.9% vs random +2.9%; A2 +13.0%; multiclass +5.2%; control +2.8%; barrier books -0.4% (A1) to +4.5% (A2). Top-20 minus universe per 20-day trade: A1 +0.07% (t 0.06), A2 +0.85% (t 0.66), control +0.01%, vs 2023-25 values of +1.16% (t 2.57), +1.16% (t 2.54) and +1.45% (t 3.05). The long edge was not confirmed, though 8 months gives expected t of about 1.2 even if the edge persisted. The bottom decile kept underperforming in 2026 (-0.74% to -0.92% vs universe), so the avoid side is the more robust half.

Gating with the absolute probability, the one advantage over relative labels. Requiring P(+1) >= 0.5 (a priori, not tuned) is ineffective for A1, where 85% of dates still have 20 or more names. For A2 (rarer +1) it acts as an exposure switch: 2023-25 Sharpe 2.18 -> 2.37 and full-period maxDD -24.6% -> -13.4%.

Shorts (F&O proxy only, since cash shorting is impossible overnight) lost money in every variant. Barrier exit: -2.2% to -5.5%/yr in 2023-25. Time exit: -19% to -23%/yr. 2026 (a down market): -4.7% to -18%. Model shorts beat random shorts by 4-7 pp/yr. Use -1 labels as avoid/exit signals for long books only. The bottom-decile 20d excess is -1.0% to -2.1% in every year.

Market-feature ablation: dropping the 10 market/regime features raises pooled AUC (0.536 vs 0.522) by removing bad timing but halves the 2023-25 time-exit portfolio edge (Sharpe 1.26 vs 2.21), while 2026 was better (+13.1%). Market features help the model learn which kind of stock wins in which regime, but that value is unstable.

Multiple testing: 432 label variants screened descriptively (144 barrier configs x 3 tau), 12 deep scorecards plus 1 control label, 6 full walk-forward runs plus one 2-fold timing test (identical numbers, discarded), 66 model x execution variants, about 130 portfolio sims at 50/80 bp with 5-seed random baselines. The SE of an annual Sharpe over 3 years is about 0.6, so the best-of-N null Sharpe excess is about 1.2-1.3 even with effective N of about 10. The observed time-exit Sharpe excess over random (+1.1 to +1.4) is borderline after deflation, consistent with the weak holdout.

Recommended absolute label spec (A1): entry open[t+1]; target +2.0 x ATR14%[t] and stop -2.0 x ATR14%[t] from entry; vertical barrier close[t+20]; stop checked before target on the same bar, gap fills at the open; +1 = target first or time return > +50 bp, -1 = stop first or time return < -50 bp, 0 otherwise; NaN outside fw.ok(20). Event rates +1 48.9 / -1 49.6 / 0 1.6 (target 43.7 / stop 41.4 / time 14.9), mean hold 9.7 bars. How to invest: rank by OOS P(+1), hold the top-20 for 20 days with a time exit or target-only take-profit, never the symmetric stop, and use the bottom decile as an avoid list. Alternative: A2 (3.0/1.5) with the P(+1) >= 0.5 gate when lower drawdown matters.
lab_issues_found: MEDIUM: portfolio_sim(exit_rule='barrier') silently drops trades whose barrier window is invalid (tr_ret NaN from later suspension, label_block or segment break). The time-exit branch has a last-available-close fallback; the barrier branch does not. This is a small look-ahead/survivorship filter (about 2% of eligible rows at h=20) affecting model and random books equally. Fix: apply the same forced-exit fallback in the barrier branch.

LOW-MEDIUM: walk_forward only scores rows whose label is non-NaN (mask & ~isnan(y)), so the investable universe already excludes names whose next-h window breaks (look-ahead, about 2%). Fix: predict on all elig_base rows in the test year and let the simulator force-exit.

MEDIUM (for comparisons): in portfolio_sim, capital released by early barrier exits sits idle at 0% until that sleeve's next turn. A1 barrier books are invested only about 50% of the time (9.7 of 20 bars), so barrier CAGR is not comparable to time-exit CAGR. Fix: report exposure, add a cash yield (Indian liquid funds about 6.5%), or redeploy.

LOW-MEDIUM: portfolio_sim books each cohort's whole-trade return at the signal date (no intra-trade mark-to-market), so maxDD is understated and by_year is attributed by entry date. Fix: daily MTM equity.

METHODOLOGICAL: for absolute labels, walk_forward's pooled AUC is dominated by the date-level timing component. It is about equal to the date-mean-only AUC every year and falls below 0.5 in 2023 and 2025 even though the per-date xs-AUC is 0.53. Fix: add per-date cross-sectional AUC / rank IC to the fold metrics.
MINOR: event_report's regime split silently labels rows with NaN mkt_dist_sma200 (1.9% of eligible rows, early 2021) as 'bear'.

MINOR: event_report's corr_monthly_pos_vs_mkt_ret uses the signal month's index return, but the label window spills into the next month. The per-date correlation with L.market_fwd(P,h) over the same window is sharper (0.72-0.87 vs 0.65-0.71). Suggest adding it to the scorecard.

COSMETIC: lablib.py docstring says prices are adjusted 'using NSE's own PREV_CLOSE field', but adjustment comes from Bc corporate-action records and PREV_CLOSE is not CA-adjusted. The brief says ~3.5M rows and 55 features; actual is 3,097,741 rows and 53 features in L.FEATURES.

headline: Rank labels remove the regime problem; market-excess sign labels only halve it. The best relative label is the per-date rank of the factor-neutral residual return (XR_neu: residual of open[t+1]->close[t+h] after OLS on beta60, vol20, log_turn20), selected on 2023-25. At h=20, long-only top-20 at 50 bps made 29.5% CAGR on dev vs 12.0% random and 15.8% Nifty 500. The 2026 holdout made +12.7% annualised vs 5.7% random and -5.7% Nifty; at 80 bps it was 24.9% dev and 8.9% holdout. Excess over random was positive in every year: +60/+209/+107/+57 bps per cohort for 2023/24/25/26; dev Newey-West t 3.13, holdout t 1.84. Most of the learned edge is the AVOID (-1) side: cross-sectional AUC 0.54-0.57 every year vs 0.48-0.54 for +1. A single-stock F&O long-short is not investable at 50/80 bps for any relative label. Status: promising, not proven (borderline after about 67 portfolio variants).

candidates.definition: Universe U = elig_base AND ISIN prefix INE (ETFs removed). r = open[t+1] -> close[t+20], adjusted prices, NaN unless fw.ok(20). Each date: OLS of r (y winsorised 1/99 for the fit only) on [1, clip(beta_60,0,3), vol_20, log_turn20] over U; residual e = r - Xb; pct = per-date percentile rank of e. Labels: +1 if pct>0.70, -1 if pct<=0.30, else 0 (20%/10% cuts also measured). Model: LightGBM regression on pct-0.5, 52 PIT features (sec_rel_mom20 excluded), L.walk_forward with date_step=2. Trade: long top-20 by OOS score every 5 days, 4 sleeves, time exit at close[t+20].

headline: Adaptive-horizon (trend-scanning) labels are not better than a plain fixed 20-day label for a 5–20 day NSE swing trader. METHOD: trend-scan |t| thresholds are not significance levels. Under a driftless iid random walk P(|t*|>=2) = 98% and P(|t*|>=5) = 67%, and the L* histogram matches real data (30% at the L=20 boundary). headline: Gating the label on classic technical setups does not help on NSE at 10 days. Breakouts, pullbacks, VCP, delivery spikes, RS leaders and gap-holds have date-matched excess within ±13 bps, and the 20d volume breakout is significantly worse (−27 bps, t=−2.7). The one gate that changes the label is a reversal gate, R1dn ("capitulation buy": close below the prior 20-day low on volume while Nifty-500 20-day momentum is negative). For R1dn, P(+1) rises from 0.450 to 0.557 and date-matched excess is +58 bps per event (month-block t=6.3, passes Bonferroni across 98 configs). It is positive in 2023, 2024 and 2025 and +75 bps in the 2026 holdout, and holds across lookbacks, volume thresholds and 5/10/20-day horizons. The effect is episodic: it sits on mass-breakdown days, the top 5 months give 60% of the excess, and holdout excess outside March 2026 is only +12 bps. Meta-labeling on top of R1dn roughly doubles per-event excess, and the every-bar model ranks gated events as well as a setup-only model. Gate plus score earns about 7–13% CAGR at 50 bps (about 5–10% at 80) at 25–36% exposure. That is the only family here that made money in the 2026 holdout, where the every-bar model lost 13% annualised. Verdict: promising, not proven. The sector-leader setup is a look-ahead leak, and every short setup is net negative.

key_findings: Label used throughout is the common primary label L.barrier_labels(h=10, pt=4.74·ATR, sl=3.16·ATR, tau=50bps), entry open[t+1]. Universe is elig_base with ISIN starting INE; this removes 49,192 ETF rows. Dev window is signals 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-16 (exits ≤ 2025-12-31); holdout is 2026-01-01 to 2026-09-10. Base label all years: +1/0/-1 = 0.444/0.061/0.494. 82% of labels exit on time (pt 6.4%, sl 11.3%), so this barrier behaves almost like a ±50 bps sign label. Monthly P(+1) std is 0.131 and its corr with the Nifty-500 monthly return is 0.65 (regime-dominated). Dev net50 is -16 bps per bar.

Event study, no model, dev. Classic long setups do not change the label once events are compared with other stocks on the same date (xs). Lift in P(+1) is 0.98-1.04. xs bps: L1 20d breakout -26.5 (t=-2.69), L2 52w -8.8, L3 pullback -3.4, L4 VCP -13.4, L5 delivery -0.7, L6 RS leader -2.2, L7 oversold-in-uptrend +3.7, L8b index leader +11.0, L9 gap-hold -35.2. Their monthly P(+1) corr with the market is 0.46-0.69, and 71-88% of events occur in bull regimes. Fresh-event variants (first firing in 10 bars) are no better.

The sector-leader setup (L8) shows +76 bps xs (t=5.45), but this is the 2026 sector-snapshot leak. Sector-known universe rows earn +29 bps vs -40 bps for NA rows per 10 days in 2023-25 (t=±5.6), and the gap disappears in 2026 (-1 vs +2). L8 is rejected. sec_rel_mom20 was dropped from all models.

The winning gate is a reversal: R1 = 20-day breakdown on volume (close < prior 20d low & volz_20 > 1), bought. Dev xs is +42 bps (t=3.0), P(+1) 0.518 vs 0.450. With the Nifty-500 20-day-momentum < 0 filter (R1dn): dev n=6,673, P(+1) 0.557 (lift 1.24), net50 +164 bps per event, xs +58 bps (month-block t=6.29). It is the only one of 98 tested configs that passes the Bonferroni hurdle of 3.48. Excess is positive in each dev year (52/49/67) and in the holdout (+75 bps, net +232 bps). In rising markets R1 has zero excess.

Robustness of R1dn. All 45 parameter variants (lookback 10/20/55, volz any/0/0.5/1/2, regime none / mkt_mom20<0 / below SMA200) have positive dev and holdout xs. Dev xs is +41/+57/+64 bps at time-exit h=5/10/20, and +111 to +119 bps over Nifty-500. Excluding data artefacts (64 events on CA, label_block or -20% rows) changes nothing. Within sector-known and sector-NA groups it beats each group's universe (+39 / +46 bps), so it is not the leak.

Main caveat: the R1 edge is episodic, a 'stock capitulation inside market capitulation'. Dev xs by number of R1 events that day: 1-2 → -59, 3-9 → -28, 10-29 → +32, 30-99 → +72, 100+ → +79 bps (12 days, +454 bps net). Isolated breakdowns continue down. There are 51 capitulation episodes in 2021-26, about 29 in dev. Top 5 months supply 60% of R1dn xs and 78% of net. Holdout excluding March 2026: xs +11.7 bps. Large-cap (fno_proxy) R1dn xs in the holdout is -48 bps. 2025 absolute net was negative (-25 bps per event) although xs was +72.

Conjunctions ('both conditions accept'): 198 configs (11 blocks + all pairs × {none, bull, mkt_dn20}). Pairs raise P(+1) to 0.56-0.63 but cut events 5-10×, and none pass Bonferroni. Examples: L7&R1 xs +103 bps (t=2.75), R1&R3|dn +102 (t=3.27). The bull filter (mkt_dist_sma200>0) only times the market; it never creates date-matched excess. L1 breakout and its conjunctions are the worst (down to -107 bps).

Short side: no short setup has positive net expectancy. Short base net is -99 bps per trade because the stop is hit 19% vs the target 2% (positive skew). The S1 breakdown short has xs -42 bps (t=-3.0), and on F&O-proxy events it loses -130 bps per trade. S5 gap-down-fail short has xs +74 bps but only 297 F&O events. The useful down-side information is the avoid list for longs: L1 breakouts (-27), L9 gap-hold (-35), S5 gap-down names held long (-69 bps xs).

Meta-labeling, 5 walk-forward runs (ALL, R1, L7, R3, L3). On a good gate the score adds PIT precision. On R1 events, a META PIT filter (score > fold training base rate) lifts P(+1) from 0.517 to 0.540 and xs from +43 to +78 bps in dev. In the holdout, P(+1) goes from 0.483 to 0.584 and xs from +53 to +118. The top tercile reaches xs +90 (dev) and +135 (holdout), the bottom tercile -15. Applying the every-bar model to R1 rows does about as well (PIT xs +67 dev, +88 holdout; date-neutral IC 0.06), since the setup-only model has only 3.3k-14k training rows. On a neutral gate (L3 pullback) the meta-model adds nothing (PIT xs -6 bps). So: gate with the setup, and rank inside it with the general model.

Every-bar model reference: daily cross-sectional AUC 0.516/0.543/0.530/0.519 and IC 0.030/0.068/0.061/0.049 for 2023-26 (dev XS-AUC t=5.2). Pooled AUC 0.518/0.558/0.484/0.544 mostly reflects timing. Top20 portfolio: full CAGR 11.4% at 50 bps (3.5% at 80), Sharpe 0.72, maxDD -29.4%, by year +44.6% / +29.3% / -12.1% / -8.9%. 2026 holdout CAGR -13.2% vs universe random -4.5% and Nifty-500 -5.7%.

Investability, time exit, 50/80 bps, random baseline ≥3 seeds. Official L.portfolio_sim with R1dn ∧ every-bar top5: CAGR 10.5% / 7.5%, Sharpe 1.24, maxDD -22.1%, mean trade +147 bps, vs +30 bps and 0.3% CAGR for random picks from the same events and -1.2% for universe random. Universe-grid slot sizing: 13.1% / 10.1%, Sharpe 1.08, maxDD -17.5%, by year +16.2% / +26.6% / -9.3% / +18.4%. Daily-entry META-PIT top5: 7.2% / 5.4%, Sharpe 1.48, maxDD -13.0%, exposure 23%. 2026 holdout: R1dn variants +7% to +27% CAGR while the every-bar model and random lost money. Selecting on dev alone would have picked the every-bar model or R3∧score (dev 17.9% / 25.7% CAGR); both lost in 2026.

Capacity and sizing: trading all R1dn events gives high per-trade expectancy (+98 bps every 5 days, +168 bps daily, dev) but CAGR of only about 1-3%. Equal weight gives light-event days full capital, and slot sizing leaves exposure too small. The edge requires sizing up on mass-breakdown days (≥30 events) and few or no positions on days with isolated breakdowns.

Answer to the role question: event-gated labeling beats labeling every bar only for the capitulation-reversal gate. Per trade it gives +106 to +155 bps net vs +53 to +59 bps for the every-bar top-k, with lower drawdown (-13% to -22% vs -29%) and a positive 2026 holdout. It is not 'proven': there are about 29 dev episodes, holdout gains are concentrated in March 2026, 2025 was negative, and sim-Sharpe of 1.0-1.5 does not clear the luck hurdle (1.38 for about 100 portfolio configs; sim Sharpe is overstated ×1.1-1.24). Classic technical setups are not worth gating on, and breakouts are worth avoiding.

How to invest: each evening, gate on close < 20d low & volz_20 > 1 & Nifty-500 20d momentum < 0. Rank gated names with the general model; take the top 5 per day or names whose score exceeds the training base rate. Use fixed slots of 2-4% of capital and scale up on mass-breakdown days. Hold 10 days with a time exit (the barrier exit is 1-3 pp CAGR worse). Run it as an overlay next to a core book, since it is in cash 65-75% of the time. Expect losing years in grinding bear markets such as 2025.

Variants tried: about 300 label/setup variants (45 event-study configs, 198 conjunctions, 45 sensitivity variants, 12 label-horizon cells), 5 walk-forward models (within the budget of 6), and about 95 portfolio configurations. The holdout was opened once and used for no selection. REPORT.md could not be saved because the harness blocks subagents from writing report files. The full narrative is in this output, the tables are in tables_autogen.md (T1-T16), and the numbers are in results.json (final_summary, s1-s11).
lab_issues_found: MEDIUM: L.walk_forward hard-codes tr.sum() < 20000 / tm.sum() < 1000 and silently skips folds. Any event-gated training set with fewer than about 60k total events gets zero folds; R1's 2023 fold has 3.3k rows. Fix: expose min_train/min_test and smaller-capacity default parameters for sparse masks. I used a documented verbatim copy with 1500/100, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 100.

MEDIUM: L.portfolio_sim builds its signal calendar from the mask's own dates (cal = np.unique(dates[m])). For sparse setup masks, step=5 then means every 5th date on which the setup fires, not every 5th trading day, and sleeve timing and CAGR become grid-dependent; R1dn results differ by several pp between the two grids. Fix: add a calendar argument (universe trading days) and book empty cohorts as cash.

MEDIUM: L.portfolio_sim equal-weights whatever picks exist, so 1 event puts 100% of a sleeve in one stock. Event strategies need fixed-slot sizing (each pick 1/top_k, rest in cash), implemented here as sizing='slot'.

HIGH (confirms E_auditor #1): the sector map is a 2026 snapshot. Sector-known rows earn +29 bps vs NA -40 bps per 10 days in 2023-25 (t=±5.6), and the gap vanishes in 2026. The sector-leader setup's +76 bps (t=5.45) is this leak; sec_rel_mom20 must be dropped.
MEDIUM (confirms E_auditor #2): elig_base contains 49,192 ETF/MF rows (ISIN INF...). Removed here with ISIN startswith 'INE'.

LOW: L.event_report by_liquidity_tercile forms terciles within the masked sample. For a setup mask this describes liquidity inside the events, not against the universe; use universe terciles per date instead.

DESIGN NOTE: the role's common barrier (pt 4.74·ATR, sl 3.16·ATR, 10 days) ends 82% of labels at the time barrier, so path-awareness is nominal. On the short side the stop is hit 19% vs the target 2%, giving short base net -99 bps per trade.
